//: LabDDB-Pro Realtime Database rules — authentication and the DDB wallet.
Deploy with:   firebase deploy --only database --project labddb-pro
(or paste into Firebase console -> Realtime Database -> Rules)
The single idea here: NOTHING in this database is writable from a browser.
Every number that represents money is moved by the Cloudflare Worker using a
service-account credential, which bypasses these rules entirely. So `.write`
is false on every path — not as a placeholder, but as the design. A student's
browser can read their own balance and never change it, which is what makes
'you are only charged for a page that printed' a property of the system rather
Reads are scoped to the owner with auth.uid == $uid. `config` is the one
public node: the cost calculator quotes a price before anyone signs in, and a
price list is not a secret.
Note that denying reads on /users means a signed-in user cannot enumerate
other students. The admin console reads the whole tree through the Worker,
which checks the caller's email on every request (see requireAdmin in
lib/api.js) rather than relying on a role stored in the database.

config.//: Pricing and limits. World-readable so the calculator works anonymously.

$uid.//: labddb-auth.js keeps a live listener here so the header chip updates the moment a print settles.
ledger.recentJobs() queries this by createdAt; without the index the REST API answers 400.
A student's own statement: top-ups in, charges out. Append-only, server-written.
Read so the UI can hide the admin link. Enforcement is server-side regardless.

openJobs.//: The reconciler's working set, keyed by jobId with no uid scoping. Server only.

printIndex.//: filename -> job. Server only: it maps a filename to the person who paid.

admin.//: Institutional UprintBD balance, reconciler state, unmatched prints. Server only.
